name: the Catholic church, three-quarter view showing one long side wall and the front vestibule
basis: As supplied to the project; the original holder and date are not confirmed.
notes: the Catholic church, three-quarter view showing one long side wall and the front vestibule. Body: rubble stone with brick trim at corners and around openings; four round/segmental-arched openings on the visible side, in order from the rear: window, narrow door, window, window, all boarded; small rectangular openings high under the eave. Roof: wood shingles, curved (barrel-like) profile with flared eaves; brick chimney on the slope near the front of the stone body; small dormer-like projection at the rear end. Front: a wooden vestibule of horizontal boards, slightly narrower than the stone body, with its own shingled round-arched roof; its end wall has two diamond-shaped panels flanking a cross shape, and a large rectangular door opening on the right part of the end wall. Open timber belfry (four posts, cross-bracing, small pyramidal shingled cap, bell wheel visible) sits on the roof where the vestibule meets the stone body. Four people (two children, one seated on a horse) and four to five saddled horses in front. Forested hill at right, a rocky peak at far left.
holder: Not established (supplied to the project; many are slides from a Victor Heritage Society talk)

name: heading "GILLETT
basis: As supplied to the project; the original holder and date are not confirmed.
notes: heading "GILLETT." "A new town platted and owned by the Beaver Park Land Company is Gillett. This town, three miles distant from Cripple Creek to the northeast, is most favorably located in the beautiful Beaver Park on Beaver Creek. A site with more picturesque surroundings could not have been chosen. Northward are the eternal snows of the Pikes Peak range and outspread below and afar toward the distant plains, the blue hills fade away. Gillett is within one and a half miles of the main center of mining operations, and from thence a down hill pull for ores coming to the stamp mills and to the railroad for transportation. At this point the Midland Terminal Railway Company will erect their ore receiving bins, shops, round houses, and a $150,000 railway hotel station, to be used also for the offices of the road. There is to be erected by Chicago capitalists a splendid resort hotel adapted for the comfort and enjoyment of pleasure seekers and tourists, and for the residents of the district. The main line of the Michigan Pipe Company to Cripple Creek is laid through Gillett and it will have waterworks from its infancy. The officials of the Beaver Park Land Company are prominent railroad men and capitalists. Mr. J. M. Parker, president of the First National Bank of Cripple Creek, is president of the company. The directors are H. Collbran, president of the Midland Terminal Railway; W."
